name: Save and resume web drafts (autosave + guest clear on success)

arm-01.note: 800ms-debounced autosave with stale-response guarding (pendingEditsRef); guest drafts keyed by HMAC-hashed random token in an httpOnly cookie; completeDraft() clears the guest cookie ONLY on successful checkout, never on abandonment — exactly matches the spec.

arm-04.note: Byte-identical to arm-01 for these files.

arm-05.note: 700ms-debounced autosave to a server draft keyed by an access token stored in sessionStorage (not httpOnly cookie — more exposed to XSS than the other arms' approach); resumes on reload via sessionStorage id. Guest-clear-on-success behavior not directly verified in the reviewed slice.

arm-06.note: Explicit design comment: signed-in customers autosave to a server draft; guests autosave to localStorage and only get a server draft + httpOnly-cookie access token at checkout identity capture; guest copy clears ONLY on success/explicit cancel, never on refresh — matches the spec intent, though guest state living in localStorage before checkout is a smaller attack surface than a cookie-backed draft from the first keystroke.

arm-01.note: Random 32-byte token minted for guests, httpOnly/sameSite=lax cookie, only the HMAC of the token stored in DB (raw token never persisted) — anti-enumeration by design since no API accepts a draft id from the client.

arm-04.note: Byte-identical to arm-01 for these files.

arm-05.note: Guest token exists and is sent via a custom x-draft-access-token header, but the raw token is kept in sessionStorage on the client rather than an httpOnly cookie — more exposed to XSS/theft than the clone cluster or arm-06's cookie-based approach.

arm-06.note: generateGuestToken/hashGuestToken/verifyGuestToken with url-safe random tokens, hashed storage, httpOnly cookie delivery, and dedicated unit checks (scripts/test-p4.mts) covering uniqueness, determinism, and rejection of wrong/null tokens.
